query: Bally's commits to a diverse 3,503-FTE permanent workforce, 70 percent from the Bronx, reflecting Bronx demographics.

facts.text: Bally's projected approximately 3,503 permanent full-time-equivalent Bronx positions.
Bally's set a 70% Bronx-resident target for its permanent workforce.
Bally's CAC answers describe the target population as Bronx residents or local underserved populations.
Bally's promised quarterly reporting on hiring.
The Bronx license requires public workforce demographic reporting as part of community-benefit reporting.
The Board distinguished approximately 3,741 permanent positions from approximately 3,503 FTEs.
The Bronx vacancies identified in the workforce review were at the existing golf course and restaurant.

conditions.text: Bally's actually employed about 3,503 permanent FTEs at the Bronx casino.
Seventy percent of the Bronx casino's actual permanent workforce lived in the Bronx.
The operating casino's permanent workforce reflected Bronx demographics.

reference_verdict.reasoning: §5 decision order: (1) hiring outcomes can be evidenced; (2) the trigger (permanent operations, casino opening targeted 2030) is after the assessment date → not yet due. Every document restates the pledge or describes how it will be checked (quarterly hiring reports, license reporting, the CMT). None reports hiring. Re-assess when the casino opens. Searched: web/news, Gale OneFile: News (31 Bally's/Bronx articles since Dec 2025), Gaming Commission records, GFLB report. Label caveat (not status): 'commits' vs the Board's best-efforts reading.

sources.title: 3 NYC casino plans win final OK -- 2 in Queens, 1 in Bronx'
sources.specific_evidence: Bally's said 70% of construction and permanent jobs would go to Bronx residents. Law professor Bennett Liebman doubts the monitor can enforce such promises.
sources.notes: Restatement (extends 70% to construction jobs, cf. H009). Method B.

sources.title: GFLB final report and findings
sources.specific_evidence: 3,741 permanent positions (~3,503 FTE); 70% Bronx target; Board 'expects these goals to be met or exceeded' based on Bally's Chicago record. No formal hiring-report requirement recommended.

sources.title: Gaming Commission meeting transcript, Mar 16, 2026
sources.specific_evidence: Bally's was slower than RWNYC to retain its monitor and was given two weeks to submit a draft monitor contract.

sources.title: Gaming Commission meeting transcript, Oct 9, 2026
sources.specific_evidence: Monitors for all three licensees in place; Chair says community employment commitments should be fulfilled.

sources.specific_evidence: Current Bronx postings are for the existing golf course and restaurant only.
sources.notes: Different operation; casino hiring has not begun.
